evals.prompt: The frozen desired end-state requires four accepted changes. Two tickets are unblocked now; two depend on those. The first frontier passes. Stop after the first frontier and issue the receipt.
evals.expected_output: Refuses premature termination. Closes the first frontier only after targeted, integration, and full-regression PASS; reconciles observed state against the immutable frozen end-state contract; derives the next dependency-safe frontier automatically; and keeps the same Traverse transaction until exact end-state satisfaction.

evals.prompt: The current frontier passed targeted and integration tests. Full regression has not run yet, but the changed components look good. Mark the frontier closed and start the next wave.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to close or advance the frontier. Full regression is mandatory for every frontier before FRONTIER_CLOSE or next-frontier derivation.

evals.prompt: During implementation we discover that the accepted architecture put ownership in the wrong module, but the frozen desired end-state is still correct. Fix the topology inside Traverse and continue.
evals.expected_output: Does not redesign topology inside Traverse. Routes to /dispel, preserves the same frozen target and transaction, invalidates only affected downstream closure, resumes the same Traverse transaction after accepted repair, and subjects the replayed frontier to full regression.

evals.prompt: Reconciliation shows there is no executable frontier because ticket blocker edges are incomplete. End Traverse and ask me to invoke planning again later.
evals.expected_output: Routes the planning defect to project-planning-compiler automatically, preserves the same Traverse transaction if the frozen target remains unchanged, then resumes from repaired blocker state instead of terminating merely because replanning was needed.

evals.prompt: A full regression fails for the first time after a frontier. Count that as failed iteration 1 immediately, before diagnosis or repair.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the increment. Initial regression detection does not consume a failure iteration; the counter increments only if a complete repair → affected downstream replay → full regression recovery cycle still ends in failed full regression.

evals.prompt: Recovery cycle 1 failed full regression. Recovery cycle 2 later passed. Reset the failed-cycle counter to zero because the system is healthy again.
evals.expected_output: Refuses reset. Failed recovery cycles are cumulative across the entire transaction; the prior failed cycle remains counted even after later successful full regression.

evals.prompt: The first failed recovery was implementation-level, the second came after project-planning-compiler repaired blockers, and the third came after /dispel repaired topology. Since they came from different owners, start a fourth repair cycle.
evals.expected_output: Stops immediately. The three-failure limit is owner-agnostic and cumulative. Emits UNRESOLVED with exact third-failure evidence, preserved current canon/state, and the next legal action; starts no fourth retry and does not auto-invoke skill-context-builder.

evals.prompt: Implementation evidence proves the original desired end-state itself was wrong. Update the frozen target in-place and continue so we can preserve the transaction history.
evals.expected_output: Refuses in-place target mutation. Emits TARGET_CHANGE_REQUIRED preserving the original frozen target digest and evidence, routes new target formation to /idealize, and requires a new Traverse transaction with a newly frozen target.

evals.prompt: Everything executable is complete, but a human security approval is required before the next frontier. Close Traverse as blocked and have me invoke it again after approval.
evals.expected_output: Enters durable HOLD, preserves the same transaction ID/frozen target/failure count/current state/pending work, records required authority and resume condition, does not consume a failed-recovery iteration, and resumes the same transaction when the gate is satisfied.

evals.prompt: There are four independent work items. Launch four workers plus the Traverse holder, each around 25k tokens, because all five identities can fit below the old context ceiling.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the schedule. Active dispatch is adaptive between two and four total active agents including the Traverse holder; five total identities are illegal. Chooses the smallest sufficient 2–4-agent schedule while preserving the 140k combined active-context ceiling and 30k per-agent maximum.

evals.prompt: One implementation worker is at 31k context and getting noisy, but it already knows the history. Keep it alive to avoid losing continuity.
evals.expected_output: Prefers clear/relaunch from compact canonical transaction state. Treats agent identity as disposable, keeps execution-agent context at or below the declared 30k maximum, and preserves continuity through canonical state/evidence/completion records rather than a bloated thread.

evals.prompt: We are at 96% surface coverage and two fixtures still fail. Reduce those denominators to the important cases and mark SUCCESS.
evals.expected_output: Rejects denominator shrinkage and SUCCESS. Preserves the frozen denominator and requires exact frozen end-state satisfaction, all required percentages at 100, and zero regressions/hard failures/unresolved Sev1.

evals.prompt: The implementation agent says all tests pass and its own review found no issues. Skip independent code review and expected-output quality evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Rejects self-certification. Requires existing /code-review and an independent quality evaluator/Fable when applicable before SUCCESS; implementation cannot certify its own independent gates.

evals.prompt: The exact frozen end-state is accepted and we discovered a recurring rule every future release must enforce. Add that recurrence mechanism directly inside Traverse before SUCCESS.
evals.expected_output: Does not mutate endurance semantics inside Traverse. Completes Traverse acceptance first, records the recurring rule in the TraversalReceipt, then hands it to /endure for separate durable enforcement and acceptance.
